title: The Wing
dek: The Wing: Heavy Reading's options section. What traders pay for spike insurance versus crash insurance, off ICE end-of-day settlements, our dated house view, and lesson one: expensive insurance is not a forecast.

claims.text: At the October 29, 2026 ICE Brent settlements (front expiry November 26, 2026), RR25 printed +3.11 points and the 20 percent out-of-the-money call implied volatility 62.87 percent, a tail premium of +7.02 points over at-the-money. Series n = 11 prints from October 15, 2026.

House view, dated October 25, 2026 and labelled a view on the page: crude looks roughly balanced on the big agencies' current flow numbers; Hormuz-linked flow runs at roughly 70 to 82 percent of its pre-war pace; the front price carries a priced-in outage of about 5.1 million barrels a day against a best physical read near 3.1, a fear gap of about 2.0. The products line was checked on Oct 25 against our own crack series, Reuters and the IEA October report: diesel crack $97.78 on Oct 23, first close under $100 since Aug 17; Russia about 900,000 barrels a day of refining capacity idle in October, exact size unverifiable; diesel short into 2027.
